newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD to await coal talks before making tax decision.
newsitem.headline: SPD to await coal talks before making tax decision.

text.p: Germany's Social Democrats (SPD) said on Monday they would await the outcome of a meeting on Tuesday between the government and miners' leaders over coal subsidies before deciding whether to rejoin cross-party tax talks.
"The resumption of talks on the tax reform will depend on the government's offer," Peter Struck, the opposition SPD's chief whip, said on the fringes of a party meeting in Berlin.

The SPD pulled out of weekend talks with the coalition on plans to cut 30 billion marks in taxes in solidarity with pit workers protesting over government plans to more than halve subsidies to Germany's loss-making coal mines.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl wants to cut federal coal aid to Germany's pits in the Ruhr and the Saarland to 3.8 billion marks by 2005 from nine billion this year.
But Struck said the alternative proposed by the IG Bergbau miners union to wind down yearly subsidies to 6.5 billion marks in 2005 was "the last offer".

"The government would be well-advised to take back its decision," Struck added. The SPD praesidium and premiers from the federal states that it rules were due to hold a further meeting in the afternoon.
